newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end up sharply at new highs, cash strong.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end up sharply at new highs, cash strong.

text.p: A stronger-than-expected trend to cash hog markets Wednesday and expectations of rising hog prices into the weekend kept CME hog futures up sharply near new contract highs at the close, traders said.
October hogs set a new high of 58.875 cents a lb and December 58.175 cents before prices finished at or near highs, up 1.025 to 0.050 higher with October up most at 58.850 cents.
Packers raised bids for cash hogs early Wednesday to encourage marketings and they will likely have to keep bids strong into the weekend to obtain adequate hog supplies, traders said.
"Packers ran short of (hog) numbers today and that furthers ideas they will be short of numbers tomorrow," said Dale Benson, Dean Witter vice president and livestock analyst.
Early indications for Thursday's cash hog prices ranged from $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt higher.
Benson also noted that producers appear to be current in their marketings. "All the indicators, as far as weights and so forth, indicate that producers are current," he said.
USDA on Friday reported the average hog weight during the week ended Sept. 28 at 249 lbs, down two lbs from the previous week and down five lbs from 254 a year ago.
Rand Financials and Cargill Investor Services were cited as strong buyers during the day, pit sources said.
In hog options, there was buying of October 58 and 59 calls late on the rally in futures, pit sources added.

Pork belly futures followed with continued good product demand cited. The lower slaughter projection for the remainder of the week and less-than-anticipated hog slaughter Wednesday was considered bullish to pork belly futures, traders said.
Hog slaughter is currently running above last year's level, but by the time Saturday kills are added, the weekly total will likely be below a year ago, Benson added.
Pork bellies already showed strength from Tuesday's bullish CME out-of-town report.

The report showed a net out-movement of 2.717 million lbs, above the high end of early estimates of out 0.5 million to 1.0 million lbs. With brisk frozen belly sales, futures need to widen the basis to cash to encourage storings next season.

"We need to go into the first of November with a basis built in, we can't be the same price as cash. Cash demand is very firm at these levels, which was shown in the CME Out-of-Town report, and that means that futures will likely go higher to widen the basis, Benson added.
Pork bellies closed 0.800 cent higher to 0.050 lower with February up most at 79.175 cents.
